blocks.text: I can describe the relationship between two factors in a ratio context.
In this lesson you will look at parts in a whole and describe how the parts are related, using the words {for every}.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A ratio shows the relative sizes of 2 or more values and allows you to compare a part with another part in a whole.
For every allows you to talk about the relative sizes of the values, e.g. for every 2 squares there is 1 triangle.

blocks.text: Here is a whole made of 3 shapes:  🟦🟦🔺
Inside the whole there are two parts, or two factors: 2 squares and 1 triangle.
**For every** 2 squares there is 1 triangle.

blocks.label: Can we say it the other way round?
blocks.text: Yes. For every 1 triangle there are 2 squares. We said the squares first because that is the order we can see them in.
Use this stem sentence: **For every** something there are something. Sometimes it is “there is” and sometimes it is “there are”.

items.title: 1 beetle, 6 legs
items.sub: For every 1 beetle there are 6 legs.

items.title: 1 pack, 10 pens
items.sub: For every 1 pack there are 10 pens.

items.title: 1 girl, 2 boys
items.sub: For every 1 girl there are 2 boys.

blocks.text: Each time we start with the one thing first.
Sometimes the parts are equal.
For every 2 balloons there are 2 party hats. We can make the numbers smaller: for every 1 balloon there is 1 party hat.
Sometimes we cannot get to a 1.
For every 2 bikes there are 3 cars. We cannot split this up any other way, so we say it just like that.
Here is a whole:  🍎🍎🍎🍌

options: For every 3 apples there is 1 banana.
For every 1 apple there are 3 bananas.
For every 3 bananas there is 1 apple.
blocks.why: There are 3 apples and 1 banana, so for every 3 apples there is 1 banana.

blocks.q: Pick the sentence that matches each picture.

options: For every 2 dogs there are 3 cats.
For every 3 dogs there are 2 cats.
For every 5 cupcakes there is 1 drink.
For every 1 cupcake there are 5 drinks.
For every 1 ice cream there are 2 cookies.
For every 1 ice cream there is 1 cookie.

blocks.text: Here is a pattern that repeats:
It is still true that for every 2 circles there is 1 square. We can see where the pattern starts and stops: 🔵🔵🟥 is the **basic pattern**, and it is repeated.

blocks.label: Is there another way to say it?
blocks.text: We could say for every 6 circles there are 3 squares. That is true too, but the simplest way is to look at the basic pattern: for every 2 circles there is 1 square.
A pattern is made like this:  ⭐⭐🔺🔺🔺  ⭐⭐🔺🔺🔺

blocks.q: Which sentence uses the basic pattern?
options: For every 2 stars there are 3 triangles.
For every 3 stars there are 2 triangles.
For every 4 stars there are 3 triangles.
blocks.why: The basic pattern that repeats is 2 stars and 3 triangles.

blocks.text: For every 2 triangles there is 1 circle. The basic pattern is  🔺🔺⚪  and it has 3 shapes.
Repeat it 5 times and you get 5 lots of 3 shapes, which is 15 shapes in total.

rows.note: 3 shapes in the basic pattern, repeated 5 times, gives 15 shapes in total.

blocks.text: In 3 × 5 = 15, the **3** is the number of shapes in the basic pattern, the **5** is the number of times the pattern is repeated and the **15** is the total number of shapes.
For every 2 triangles there is 1 circle. Could there be 14 shapes? 21 shapes? 99 shapes?
Each basic pattern has 3 shapes, so the total has to be made of whole lots of 3.
It is possible if the total number of shapes is a **multiple of 3**.

blocks.label: Tap to check the three totals
blocks.text: 21 is a multiple of 3 (7 lots of 3), so it is possible. 99 is a multiple of 3 (33 lots of 3), so it is possible. 14 is not a multiple of 3, so it is not possible.
A pattern is made from 2 squares and 3 circles. The basic pattern has 5 shapes, so the total must be a multiple of 5.

blocks.q: Could the pattern have this many shapes in total?

options: Yes, possible
No, not possible
Yes, possible
No, not possible
Yes, possible
No, not possible
Yes, possible
No, not possible

blocks.q: For every 3 red counters there is 1 blue counter. The basic pattern has 4 counters. Sort the totals.

slides.title: Watch out! Repeat, don’t add on

blocks.text: For every 2 squares there is 1 triangle. What if we repeat the pattern 2 times?
🟦🟦🔺  🟦🟦🔺  gives 4 squares and 2 triangles.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Do not add on to link the parts. To keep the same ratio, repeat the whole basic pattern: 2 repeats means 2 × 2 = 4 squares and 2 × 1 = 2 triangles.
You can use two shapes or two colours of cubes and 24 in total. Which ratios will work?
The ratio will work if the number of shapes in the basic pattern is a **factor of 24**.

blocks.label: Try an example
blocks.text: A basic pattern of 6 shapes works: 6 × 4 = 24, so the pattern is repeated 4 times. A basic pattern of 5 shapes does not work, because 24 is not a multiple of 5.

slides.title: Describe the relationship between two factors in a ratio context

items: Ratios describe the relationship between parts in a whole.
Repeating patterns can be described using the language of ratio: **for every** …
Look for the basic pattern that repeats and describe it simply.
If you know the ratio, you can work out how many parts there are in the whole.

flashcards.back: The relative sizes of 2 or more values. It lets you compare a part with another part in a whole.

flashcards.front: What do the words “for every” help you do?
flashcards.back:
Talk about the relative sizes of the values.

For every 2 squares there is 1 triangle.
For every 2 squares there is 1 triangle.

flashcards.front: A beetle has 6 legs. Describe 1 beetle and its legs using “for every”.
flashcards.back: For every 1 beetle there are 6 legs.

flashcards.front: A pack contains 10 pens. Describe 1 pack and its pens using “for every”.
flashcards.back: For every 1 pack there are 10 pens.

flashcards.front: For every 2 balloons there are 2 party hats. How can you make the numbers smaller?
flashcards.back: For every 1 balloon there is 1 party hat.

flashcards.front: What is the basic pattern of a repeating pattern?
flashcards.back: The simplest part that is repeated.

flashcards.front: A basic pattern has 3 shapes and is repeated 5 times. How many shapes in total?
In 3 × 5 = 15 for a repeating pattern, what does the 5 stand for?
flashcards.back: The number of times the pattern is repeated.

flashcards.front: For every 2 triangles there is 1 circle. When is a total number of shapes possible?
flashcards.back: When the total is a multiple of 3, because the basic pattern has 3 shapes.

flashcards.front: You use 24 shapes in total. When will a ratio work?
flashcards.back: When the number of shapes in the basic pattern is a factor of 24.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Describe the relationship between two factors in a ratio context
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a number or a short word. Think about the basic pattern and how many times it is repeated.

questions.prompt: A basic pattern has 3 shapes. It is repeated 5 times. How many shapes are there in total?
A pattern is made from 2 squares and 3 circles. How many shapes are in the basic pattern?
The basic pattern is 2 squares and 3 circles. It is repeated 4 times. How many shapes are there in total?
questions.explanation: The basic pattern has 5 shapes and 5 × 4 = 20.

questions.prompt: The basic pattern is 2 squares and 3 circles. It is repeated 4 times. How many circles are there in total?
questions.explanation: There are 3 circles in each basic pattern and 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.prompt: For every 3 squares there is 1 hexagon. How many hexagons go with 9 squares?
questions.explanation: 9 squares is 3 lots of 3 squares, so there are 3 hexagons.

questions.prompt: For every 3 boys there are 4 girls. How many children are in the basic pattern?
For every 2 triangles there is 1 circle. Could there be 21 shapes in total? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: The basic pattern has 3 shapes and 21 is a multiple of 3 (7 × 3 = 21).

questions.prompt: For every 2 triangles there is 1 circle. Could there be 14 shapes in total? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: The basic pattern has 3 shapes and 14 is not a multiple of 3.

questions.prompt: You use 24 shapes in total. The basic pattern has 6 shapes. How many times is it repeated?
questions.explanation: 6 × 4 = 24, so the pattern is repeated 4 times.

questions.prompt: For every 2 balloons there are 2 party hats. Complete the simplest sentence: for every 1 balloon there is ___ party hat.
questions.explanation: The parts are equal, so for every 1 balloon there is 1 party hat.
